newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein President Adams hurt in car crash.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein President Adams hurt in car crash.

text.p: Gerry Adams, head of the Irish Republican Army's (IRA) political wing, Sinn Fein, was injured in a car crash in Ireland, his spokesman said on Thursday.
"He was badly shaken. He suffered shock and some bruising but he's now back in Belfast again. He was in hospital for a few hours," the spokesman said of Adams.
Adam's car collided with another vehicle on Wednesday.
Sinn Fein, which seeks to end British rule in Northern Ireland, has offices in Belfast and Dublin and Adams is a frequent traveller on the 100-mile (160km) road between the two cities.
The 48-year-old politician has cancelled engagements in coming days to recuperate, the spokesman said. "He is taking some time off to recover and will be back at work in due course."
Adam's party is the political wing of the Irish Republican army which has waged a 27-year war against British rule and ended a 17-month ceasefire in February.
Full details of the accident were not known.
